title: Audio-Modality Safety Benchmark for Speech-Input Models
original_idea: Generate 150-200 harmful prompts in both text and synthesized audio (using TTS). Run through a speech-LLM pipeline and measure refusal rate for audio-sourced inputs vs. direct text inputs.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Audio attack surfaces are under-explored, but the pipeline (TTS -> STT -> LLM) may not reveal fundamental safety issues if the STT step faithfully transcribes.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires setting up TTS, speech-to-text, and LLM pipelines. Multiple modality-specific tools add significant setup complexity for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 150-200 prompts through a multi-stage pipeline. The pipeline itself is the complexity; the experiment design is clear.

novelty.reasoning: JALMBench (arXiv:2505.17568, 2025) benchmarks jailbreak vulnerabilities in audio language models, finding 21.5% ASR for non-adversarial harmful queries and 96.2% ASR for AdvWave attacks. SACRED-Bench evaluates robustness under complex audio-based attacks (66% ASR even on Gemini 2.5 Pro). Chat-Audio Attacks (CAA) provides four distinct audio attack types. SpeechGuard (Amazon) explores adversarial robustness of multimodal LLMs for speech. The proposed 150-200 prompt TTS-based benchmark is directly subsumed by these existing, more comprehensive benchmarks.
